properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 14 at 10:37AM CDT until September 14 at 4:30PM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Andrew County in northwestern Missouri...
Southeastern Holt County in northwestern Missouri...

* WHEN...Until 430 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks, streams, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1034 AM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms occurred early this morning.
Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the warned
area. Between 3 and 7 inches of rain have fallen across the
warned area.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Savannah, Oregon, Forest City, Fillmore, Rosendale and Rea.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL 430 PM CDT THIS AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Hamilton, KS; Kearny, KS; Stanton, KS
properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 14 at 2:46PM CDT until September 14 at 3:45PM CDT by NWS Dodge City KS
properties.description:
SVRDDC

The National Weather Service in Dodge City has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southern Hamilton County in southwestern Kansas...
Southwestern Kearny County in southwestern Kansas...
Northwestern Stanton County in southwestern Kansas...

* Until 345 PM CDT/245 PM MDT/.

* At 246 PM CDT/146 PM MDT/, a severe thunderstorm was located 13
miles northwest of Johnson City, moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Kendall.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.areaDesc: Pamlico Sound; Neuse and Bay Rivers
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 14 at 3:49PM EDT until September 14 at 5:15PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
SMWMHX

The National Weather Service in Newport has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Neuse and Bay Rivers...
Pamlico Sound...

* Until 515 PM EDT.

* At 349 PM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located near The Mouth Of
The Neuse River, moving southwest at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
The Vicinity Of Hancock Creek, The Vicinity Of Slocum Creek, The
Vicinity Of Clubfoot Creek, Oriental, Mid Point Of Cherry
Branch-Minnesott Beach Ferry Terminal, The Mouth Of The Neuse
River, The Vicinity Of Adams Creek, and The Vicinity Of South
River.
properties.instruction:
Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.
Wind gusts to 40 knots, high waves, dangerous lightning, and heavy
rain are possible with this storm.

properties.areaDesc: Citrus, FL; Levy, FL; Marion, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 14 at 1:40PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Tampa Bay Ruskin has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.Elevated water levels are expected along the river over the next
several days due to recent heavy rainfall.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...From this afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:45 PM EDT Monday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon and continue rising to 28.2 feet this afternoon.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT FROM THIS AFTERNOON UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 14 at 1:49PM MDT until September 14 at 2:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
SVRABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Central Rio Arriba County in north central New Mexico...

* Until 215 PM MDT.

* At 149 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 12 miles south of
Heron Lake State Park, or 29 miles southwest of Tierra Amarilla,
moving east at 20 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of Central Rio Arriba County.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.
